title: TransitionGuard
summary: Scan React and CSS source offline for View Transition usage and duplicate static view-transition-name declarations.
problem: Developers adopting View Transitions can accidentally reuse a custom view-transition-name across elements, causing transitions to be skipped when those elements render together.
audience: Frontend developers adding React or browser View Transitions to existing web applications.
why_now: React 19.3 made ViewTransition and addTransitionType stable on September 9, 2026, while current MDN guidance requires custom view-transition-name values to be unique for rendered elements participating in a transition.
difference: TransitionGuard is a zero-dependency read-only inventory focused specifically on View Transition names, classes, React component usage, and transition types across a local codebase.
monetization_hypothesis: Best kept as a free local developer utility; a paid team dashboard or editor integration would need separate demand validation.
limitations: A static duplicate can be harmless when the matching elements can never render at the same time.
Dynamic names and runtime DOM state are outside this scanner's scope.

alternatives.name: Stylelint
alternatives.difference: Stylelint is a general CSS linter with configurable rules; TransitionGuard provides a focused cross-file View Transition inventory with React usage and duplicate-name reporting out of the box.

alternatives.name: ESLint
alternatives.difference: ESLint analyzes JavaScript/TypeScript but does not inspect CSS view-transition-name declarations and React View Transition usage together.
